utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And what about the chief of security; was he linked to the chief of staff or the commander? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If the chief of security was linked to the commander, would the military police not have to be linked to the commander too? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: In this variant, I thought the link was to the commander, and then the military police was linked to the commander through the chief of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could he also be linked to the chief of staff and the commander, according to this chart, the way it looks - thank you - or is this some sort of mistake? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: It's possibly a mistake on account of speed, on account of one's inability to regulate this over a very short period of time. So an error probably occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, can you now look at the link between the commander and the battalions 1 through 8? The Podrinje Battalion and its platoons, you can see the division here in the third column and the fourth column, Anti-Aircraft, Light Self-Propelled Artillery Division, Anti-Aircraft, Engineering Company, and this battalion here. My question is: Was any unit left out here that was directly linked to the commander, and if so, please tell which one? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: I can't remember if there is another unit that belongs here not being reflected. Somebody drew this chart. Maybe they left something out. I can't remember. I can't remember whether there's anything else that should be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you bring this chart along with you when you spoke to Mr. Manning? Did you draw it right there and then in front of him? How was it produced? Somebody wrote something down and then you added to it? What can you tell the Chamber about how the chart came about, how it was produced? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: I don't know how the chart was produced, but it was added to during the interview. More drawings were made and names were added to it, too, but I did not produce this chart myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you add all these things that are written here in pen and in the Latinic script?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you add this here, that the Military Police Company was linked to the chief of security?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this your handwriting down towards the bottom of the chart, just outside the frame where it says "The 21st of September, 2001"? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: Yes, right after the date. I don't know whose signature that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does it not say "Mihajlo"?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: Yes, but right after that, to the right, no, it's not. I don't know who wrote that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Would that be Dean Manning initialling the page which you gave to him?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: I don't know that, I don't know whether he did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, sir, can you mark with a number 1 where it says "Military Police Company," part of the organisational chart of the chief of staff, and with a number 2, where you say it was under the chief of security, and with a number 3, mark where it says when you provided this chart with your signature. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the Court Usher, please. Please, number 1 next to "Military Police Company."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And number 3, where it says when you provided this chart with your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What about your microphone. Once again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: What is the number 1 in reference to, and then the number 2, and then the number 3? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, could this please be admitted, the chart as marked, and reflecting the changes made by the witness? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This marked chart will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1111, marked by the witness in court for the second time today, shall be assigned Exhibit D297. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us this too, sir, Mr. Galic: To the best of your knowledge and recollection, would the Military Police Company have to be linked directly to the commander in order to be directly subordinated to him? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure and I can't say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please look at P1108, in that case, P1108.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at what you said to the investigator when you spoke to him, where the company should be. Thank you. There you go. That's the interview that you conducted -- or that Dean Manning conducted with you on the 27th of June, 2002. That's what line 3 says, the date. And in the line 2, it says who conducted the interview with you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think we could have the same version across our screen, because this is a bilingual interview with parts in English and parts in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, I see it like you explained it. And the specific part could be enlarged if you give an indication where you will read from. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now have page 45, please. 45, that's the page we want to be looking at. The lower half of page 45 in English, in Serbian. There you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The investigator asks you: "Who did he tell that to?" And you say: "At the officers' briefing, one of the officers' briefings, where the senior officers were present, he announced his decision, this order that security, chief of security, would report to his superior but within the structure of the corps and the Main Staff." Did you see that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I said that, but this was in reference to sending reports to one's superior command by the brigade command and by the security officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please -- you spoke about the instructions; right? Let's go back to the instructions to see whether that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the third paragraph up from the bottom on the same page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The third paragraph from the bottom up, Mihajlo Galic says: "No, no, no, he didn't say that. He only said that they were responsible for their work to their direct superior in the Supreme Command."

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: This was only in reference to the drafting of the reports for the command, like the previous thing that we looked at, so that's what they were talking about and no other activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Page 46, let's see what you say in the continuation of this same interview. The investigator wanted to clarify some issues with you, who could take manpower from the Military Police Battalion. Now, he asks you: "Does that mean that, for example, the security officers, in case of need, could use the manpower, take men, vehicles, and anything else from the brigade without reporting about it or, indeed, consulting the brigade commander?" And then you said: "The last time around on the 21st, I said that the chief of security had, as his subordinated units, also the military police unit, and he was to exercise command and control over it." And then the next time you talk, you say: "Through the commander of that unit." And now the investigator is asking you this: "And my question was: Could he take resources -- could the chief of security take resources from the brigade, use them, and not tell the brigade command?" And you go on to answer: "No, that should not have been the case, with the exception of the military police unit. The military police, yes; the rest, no. I assume that is the case, but I'm not sure." Thank you. Bearing in mind the rules we read, could the security organ take from the military police some officers without telling the commander, since we saw that the commander was in command of the military police when we looked at the military police rules? If so required, we might as well go back to it so you can have another look. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: No, no need for that. I never studied the rules. I thought it worked like this. I thought it worked as I said during the interview. And that's all I can do, that's the best I can do. Chief of security of the Military Police Company, it was just that once, so I believed that the chief could decide about the manpower. When an individual led the unit, then he could have the individual brought over, secured, and so on and so forth, and that's why I said what I said at the time. Had I had the rules, a copy of the rules right in front of me, had I known what I know now, it probably would have been different.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that you've read the rules, how would you qualify the situation now? How should it be different, and who should be the commander of the military police? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: As I said many times, it's all under the command of the brigade commander. Well, now the battalion commanders are in charge of their own battalions, the division commander is in charge of their divisions, the military police company, and so on and so forth. I believe that it was in addition to the chief of security and that he had certain powers, and that he had the authority to command -- or, rather, use -- or, rather, take some of those men for some of those tasks performed by the Military Police Company, and that's all I knew.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Since you know now, can we have D202. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Rules on the Responsibilities. Can you please look at the title. It reads "Regulations on the Responsibilities of the Land Army Corps Command in Peacetime."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please go to page 3 of the English and page 4 in the B/C/S. There, we can see that. Can we please zoom in. Thank you. There. "Regulations on the Responsibilities of the Land Army Corps Command in Peacetime." And then Article 1 reads: "These regulations prescribe the responsibilities of the Land Army Corps Command. "According to the regulations, the definition of responsibilities shall comprise the rights, obligations, and scope of work of command organs and officers of these organs in the execution of the stipulated work and tasks." Can you now please look at Article 4 and what it says: "Command organs and their officers shall execute work within the scope of responsibility on the basis of the law and other regulations passed pursuant to the law ..." And then the next page, please: "Documents from the competent levels of command and control, as well as provisions of these regulations --" "Provisions of these regulations," I'm sorry, that was a "regulations."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: These are regulations; right? And now the third paragraph on page 2 reads: "Command organs may not transfer tasks in their scope of responsibility to other command organs, nor may they take on the tasks of an appropriate organ of a superior or subordinate command, unless they are specially authorised to do so." My question is: We see what the regulations say. Would he have been authorised to transfer his right further up or further down, in keeping with these regulations? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: General, sir, I've never studied these rules and regulations. I did what I was ordered to do, and that was all. I was told exactly what to do. And this is not something that was part of my job. I don't know this, nor, indeed, did I ever find out about this. I simply never came across this. I didn't have a copy of these regulations. I don't think I've ever set eyes on them, as a matter of fact. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that the same relationship exists in the corps command and in the brigade command? Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about the corps. I can talk about the brigade. I really am not familiar with any of the superior units or commands.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's look at page 7 in Serbian and page 6 in English. Thank you. Please zoom in for the benefit of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let's look at Article 9 of "Special Provisions," where it says "Commander." Paragraph 2 of "Special Provisions," Article 9 - we can see it in English as well - I quote: "The commander shall command and control subordinate units and institutions within the scope of the responsibility he received. He shall be responsible to his superior for his work and the situation and subordinate units and institutions and for proper and timely execution of work and tasks in the competence of the command organ." My question is this: Does this apply to your command as well? Did your commander command and control subordinated units and institutions in the brigade within the scope of the responsibility he received, and did he transfer his responsibility on to others?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: I really don't know how to answer your question. How do I analyse this in order to be able to answer your question? Please, I cannot speak from the level of the brigade commander or the corps commander. I can't tell you what were their responsibilities, whether they transferred their competences and responsibilities on to their subordinates. It's a matter unknown to me. I don't want to get involved in that. I never knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm not asking you this for no reason. In your statement, you said that competences were transferred on to the security organ, in terms of the military police. That's what you stated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at page 6 -- or, rather, page 7 in English and 8 in Serbian. Let's look at that. Thank you. Let's look at page 8 in Serbian and page 7 in English. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We're looking at Article 6 on the page that you're looking at, and I'm quoting for you. These are all authorities of the commander: "Managing the security service, being responsibile for the security of the command and subordinate units and institutions, and taking measures on the basis of regulations and his responsibility." This is Article 9, bullet point 6. Could your brigade commander transfer his authorities and responsibilities on to somebody else? I'm talking about managing the security service and being responsibile for the security of the command.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: This is the rule of corps command. Please don't ask me about transfer of responsibilities. You're reading articles and rules for corps command. I've told you already that I know nothing about that. I had a list of the activities that I was supposed to carry out. This is just too high up for me. I can't talk about corps, the Main Staff. I can't analyse that. I can't tell you whether somebody had this or that right or responsibility. I've never come across a thing like this before.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, first of all, no overlap, please. And the second concern I want to mention is: This witness has now, several times, told you that he is not familiar with these rules, that he can't testify about these rules, he never studied them. You should focus on those areas of his testimony he is familiar with. Otherwise, it could be a waste of time. You will probably receive again and again the same answer. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Within the brigade, I did maintain the VOB-8 log-book. I've never seen that in the corps command. I know that I did it in brigade, that many others before me and after me did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you explain, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, what VOB-8 is? What does the abbreviation stand for, and what kind of information does VOB-8 contain?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: This is information for soldiers. Now, after 15 years, I really can't remember what information it contained. I know that there was the name, the first and the family name, the military specialty. Please, you have to understand that I did what I did not because I liked it, but because I had to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you ever duty-bound to send your reports to the corps command about what your organ was doing and what the strength of your unit was based on the information contained in VOB-8?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: Reports were sent about the strength of the unit regularly according to a schedule which was given to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. When it comes to your superior commands, did they have the same schematic, the same structure, the same obligations, when it came to the filling out of "VOB-8" box, or did other brigades do it differently?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: General, sir, I was a member of the Zvornik Brigade. I know how things were done, in principle, in my brigade. And as for the others, I was never a member of any other brigade. I could never control how they did things. I didn't have an insight into how they did things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please wait. Now continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you have to send your reports to the brigade, and did you have to tally your reports with the reports of other brigades so as to make them uniform with other brigades and corps? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: General, sir, we sent reports about the strength of the brigade for our brigade. How others did it, whether they did it or not, I don't know. I only know that we sent our reports at the intervals that were requested from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you also use all the forms, such as VOB-8, which is a form? Are they used at the same time in brigades and in corps? Did you know that? And in your work, did you have that in mind when you sent your reports?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: I can only assume that all units had to do that in an identical way, that those VOB forms had to be filled out and contain information on all unit members. I suppose that that was the case, but I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your answer. And can we now look at page 10 in Serbian and page 8 in English. Thank you. Article 10 of the same regulations, that's at the very beginning. Can it be zoomed in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: It says: "The chief of staff shall replace the commander when the latter is absent and shall have all rights and duties. If the commander and the chief of staff are both absent at the same time, the commander shall be replaced by the officer assigned on the order of the commander." My question is this: You have just told us that Vinko Pandurevic was absent between the 4th and the 15th, to the best of your recollection. Would you say that Article 10 applied, that the chief of staff shall replace the commander when the latter is absent? So was that the case during the relevant period of time? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: When the commander was absent, he was replaced by the chief of staff. When both were absent, as far as I know, it never happened in our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this envisaged by the regulations? It did not need to happen in your brigade, but could it, for example, happen that one was on sick leave and the other was away on business? Is there a rule that envisages such a situation?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm looking at Article 10, and I can see that this, indeed, is envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, while we still have this document on the screen in e-court, can we look at page 30 in English and page 35 in Serbian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We are looking at Article 7 of this regulation that deals with security organ. Actually, it's Chapter 7. Article 29 of that chapter says, and I quote: "The security organ is a specialised organ of the command for organising and implementing security measures and undertaking other specialised work in the field of security that is placed under its responsibility by special regulations and is, in this regard, responsible for: "Uncovering and preventing intelligence and other subversive activities of foreign intelligence ..." And so on and so forth. You can read that for yourself. You can see everything.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now let's quickly go to paragraph 9 of Article 29. Could you please quickly show us that bullet point, and then I'll have a question for the witness, where it says: "Expertly directing security organs and the military police in the corps command and units and in other JNA units in the zone of responsibility, organising, directing and co-ordinating their activities, providing assistance, and controlling their work, especially in regard to counter-intelligence work and tasks."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And my question is this: Did you have in mind this, when you said there were exceptions to every rule, or did you have something else in mind? If the latter is correct, can you please explain, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, what it was? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: What was read to me were the duties of the security organ of the corps, and I repeat, again and yet again, that I never saw this before, I never read this before. I will never have an opportunity to do it, given my age and everything else. I can't give you any comment with this regard. These are someone's duties, and I can't tell you anything about it because I don't know anything about this. The only thing I can do is just read, and I can tell you I don't know, I'm not familiar, I've never seen -- whether this was, indeed, the case in the brigade command, I don't know. I was never in a security organ, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Who was in control of what?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: Regarding the article you mentioned, there's a lot more of those. I really can't, I'm sorry. I'm not familiar with the subject-matter. I find it very difficult to find my way around. Any further reading of these corps rules and who was in charge of what is really not helping. I'm not familiar with the substance; it's that simple. I don't know what approach to take when this is read back to me and then you ask me whether this was the case or whether something else was the case. This wasn't my job. I'm not familiar with it. It's very hard for me. It's very unnatural, if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the record, lines 13 and 14 on page 78 are part of the answer of the witness. That was not the question of Mr. Tolimir. Mr. Tolimir, you have a few minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's look at D294, which was tendered at the beginning of our conversation, page 7 of that document. This is page 8 in English, the bottom of the page. Thank you very much, Aleksandar. The end of page 8 in the English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Galic, I'm not angry with you because you don't know the rules. But should you not have said that to the investigators and lawyers when they asked you about the authorities of certain organs that you weren't familiar with, such as this: The third entry "Petrusic," "Petrusic," "Galic," "Petrusic," "Galic," and then you say -- "Petrusic," "Galic": "Therefore, we may conclude that in relation to the category of personnel, the company commander was Miomir Jasikovac in July 1995, and his superior officer along the same line, Drago Nikolic, Colonel [as interpreted] Drago Nikolic?" And your answer was: "Yes." And then he goes on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, just a correction for the record. You said, I quote: "And then you say ..." And then the question was quoted by you, but it was not Witness Galic who said that but Mr. Petrusic, the Defence counsel. This is a correction to page 79, line 12, at the end of the line. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one additional correction for the record. It says in the English version, at least, that it's Lieutenant Drago Nikolic, whereas I think the record shows "Colonel Drago Nikolic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I see "Lieutenant Drago Nikolic" in the translation in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, I was referring to the current transcript on LiveNote, where it says, at line 18 of page 79 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. In the document, itself, it says "Lieutenant Drago Nikolic." Thank you for the correction. Mr. Tolimir, I think we have to conclude the hearing of today. It's 7.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just asking a question based on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Galic, had you been familiar with the rules, would you have answered the same way, the question asked by Attorney Petrusic and earlier by Investigator Manning?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: I said what I knew. When I didn't know something, I didn't discuss it. I said what I knew at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: But you go on to say: "Yes, that's right," which means you answer as if you knew? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: Because that's what Petrusic told me, the same thing, so that's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Just tell us one thing. Did you -- were you led by his question, and that was why you answered the way you answered, or did you really believe that it was like that.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO GALIC
utterances.text: I was probably led by the nature of the question, and then I simply said, Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Galic. I wish you a very good rest. Don't be angry with me. We'll continue tomorrow, but you understand I need to ask you all these questions for the record, because all these documents were admitted as OTP documents and they constitute evidence in a court of law. Thank you very much. Have a nice rest and see you back here tomorrow. Thank you very much, Mr. Galic. Thank you, everyone. I'm sorry for continuing for longer than normally required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, we have to adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, in the afternoon, at 2.15 in Courtroom III. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 5th day of July, 2011, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24 25
